correctness.rationale: The polynomial-in-binomial-basis Cartier transformations follow from B(x)=B(x^2)/(1-x)^2; exactly 100 reachable states are exhaustively generated and the 16,384 independent Euler-product comparisons agree. Eight targets have exact 100-dimensional zero certificates for (T-I)(T-2I) at depths >=11, so Cayley-Hamilton proves all-depth histogram formulas from two initial rows. A second dimension-100 certificate proves exactly 10 unstable low-bit suffixes for every depth >=7; arbitrary aligned dyadic blocks therefore differ by at most 10 from the initial-block 112 count, and binary decomposition gives O(log X) discrepancy and genuine ordinary natural density 1/32. Every 112 value is 16(8m+7), excluded by Legendre. Computations are reproducible with embedded verify.py; tests alone are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact all-level eight-residue histogram is a natural quantitative invariant of the classical two-color binary partition function. The stable-suffix structure yields ordinary frequency 1/32 with logarithmic discrepancy for an explicit Legendre obstruction, improving the known two-progression 1/64 lower bound by a factor two. It contributes a concrete significant density theorem to the general-color questions identified by Sobolewski–Ulas rather than a routine substitution or sample.
